resources.string: Subtitles and translation on top of any app
Captions whatever is playing on the phone. Some apps (calls, certain streaming and music apps) block audio capture — use Microphone for those.
Captions speech around you, or the phone\'s own speaker.
Reads each translated sentence aloud while wired or Bluetooth headphones are connected.
Choose a language under \"Translate to\" to hear it spoken.
Headphones connected. The translation will be spoken in them.
No headphones connected. Captions still show; the voice starts when you connect wired or Bluetooth headphones.
No %1$s voice is installed, so the translation will not be spoken. Add one in Settings → Text-to-speech output.
Ready. Language models download on first use, then everything except Gemini runs offline.
Captions are running. Switch to any app.
Free, and works offline after a one-time download of about 30 MB. Fast, but less accurate than Gemini.
Lower other sound while the voice speaks

Most accurate, for every language: Gemini reads each sentence in the context of the ones before it and works out misheard words. The caption text (not the audio) is sent to Google with your own key, so it needs internet. Get a free key at aistudio.google.com/apikey. Free keys allow only a few requests per minute, so finished sentences are sent first, together when several are waiting, and the sentence in progress is refreshed at most every 6 seconds.

Works without internet after a one-time 910 MB download (use Wi-Fi). Slower and less accurate than Gemini: the Khmer line appears a few seconds after each sentence ends. Needs a phone with about 6 GB of RAM or more.
Enter your Gemini API key, or choose \"On this phone\".
Audio recording permission is required to transcribe speech.
Allow \"Display over other apps\" so captions can float on top, then tap Start again.
